# Current state — bpg-rs

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

### bpg-hevc-decode

`active` · `@bpg.term.bpg-hevc-decode/1` · scope `path "crates/bpg-hevc-decode/**"`

The pure-Rust HEVC still-image intra decoder crate: CABAC, intra
prediction, transform/dequant, deblocking, and SAO. AGENTS.md's own
prose names this crate `bpg-hevc-decode` in one sentence and then
refers to its tests at `crates/bpg-decode/tests` in the same
sentence — a naming lag in the source document, preserved here
rather than silently normalized.

### bpg-tools

`active` · `@bpg.term.bpg-tools/1` · scope `path "crates/bpg-tools/**"`

The CLI crate exposing `encode`, `decode`, and comparison/development
tools; the installed end-user binary built from it is named `bpgenc`.

### still265

`active` · `@bpg.term.still265/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/**"`

The Rust-native HEVC still-image encoder crate, shaped after x265's
all-intra still-picture path but not a direct transplant of x265's
frame encoder.

### Support crates

`active` · `@bpg.term.support-crates/1` · scope `path "crates/bpg-bitstream/**"`, `path "crates/bpg-format/**"`, `path "crates/bpg-image/**"`

`bpg-bitstream`, `bpg-image`, and `bpg-format` hold shared primitives
used by the encoder and decoder: container varints and bit I/O, image
planes and color-space conversion, and BPG container header
read/write, respectively.

## Constraints

### Every optimization claim is byte-identical, decision-neutral, or decision-affecting

`active` · `@bpg.constraint.decision-class-taxonomy/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/**"`

Any change to still265's search or encode path must be classified
into exactly one of three classes before it can be promoted, and
each class carries its own required gate: byte-identical changes
need a hash match across a resolution/QP/threading matrix;
decision-neutral changes need a BD-rate sweep showing |BD| at or
below about 0.05%; decision-affecting changes need a full
multi-image BD-rate and quality narrative and must never be
described as "free speed".

### psy-rd/psy-rdoq must be byte-identical when both are zero

`active` · `@bpg.constraint.psy-zero-cost-when-off/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/stillsearch/**"`

When both `psy_rd` and `psy_rdoq` are 0.0, the encode must be
byte-identical to the pre-psy encoder. All new psychovisual work is
guarded behind `psy_rd > 0` / `psy_rdoq > 0`.

## Policies

### Commits are scoped to one behavior or subsystem

`active` · `@bpg.policy.commit-scoping/1` · scope `all` · topic `commit-scoping`

Recent commits use concise, imperative subjects with an optional
crate prefix. Commits stay scoped to one behavior or subsystem. Pull
requests describe the codec behavior changed, list commands run,
mention relevant env vars, and link any issue or comparison data.

### Environment toggles follow BPG_* naming

`active` · `@bpg.policy.env-toggle-naming/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/**"` · topic `env-toggle-naming`

Environment toggles follow `BPG_*` names, for example
`BPG_ENC_THREADS`, `BPG_TILES`, and `BPG_PRIMITIVES`.

### Codec changes get exact reconstruction or round-trip tests

`active` · `@bpg.policy.testing-conventions/1` · scope `path "crates/**/tests/**"` · topic `testing-conventions`

Favor exact reconstruction or round-trip assertions for codec
changes, and include focused regressions for bitstream features such
as tiles, WPP, SAO, AQ, chroma formats, and bit depths. When changing
one crate, run its targeted tests first, then broader workspace
tests when practical.

## Assessments

### The 2x gap is architecture, not over-searching

`verified` · `@bpg.assessment.headline-diagnosis/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/**"`

The candidate funnel is already at x265 parity or better. The
remaining wall-clock gap is not "searching too much per CU" - it is
(1) one whole CU depth x265 never evaluates, (2) a WPP
implementation that clones the full reconstruction frame per row
claim, (3) an RDOQ/rate-costing kernel family that runs in scalar
f64 against x265's fixed-point int64 plus assembly, and (4) the
overlay/border architecture vs x265's contiguous recon planes.

### The residual 12 MP gap is parallel scheduling, not kernel throughput

`verified` · `@bpg.assessment.parallel-efficiency-not-kernels/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/write.rs"`

The remaining speed difference is not a general kernel-throughput
deficit: per-thread kernel work is at parity or better on the
worst 12 MP image. The residual gap is mainly parallel scheduling
efficiency and image-content sensitivity on the hybrid i7-13700H,
which motivated capping WPP worker count at the performance-core
thread count on narrow wavefronts.

**supported_by** `@bpg.observation.wpp-idle-time/1`

See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#the-residual-12-mp-gap-is-parallel-scheduling-not-kernel-throughput).

### RDOQ coefficient selection is not the quality lever

`verified` · `@bpg.assessment.rdoq-selection-refuted/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/rdoq.rs"`

RDOQ coefficient SELECTION is not the lever for the still265-vs-C
quality gap - this refutes the prior leading hypothesis. RDOQ was
measured mean 1.5% above the local optimum (hard-quant 5.1% above),
and a coordinate-descent refinement experiment on top of it was
RD-negative. Strategic conclusion, from reading x265 source: there
is no missing x265 algorithm; the ~1.5x wall gap is distributed
per-call implementation efficiency, and the quality gap is
partition-independent, search-independent, and filter-independent.

### The architectural risk was early cheap-top-1 finalization, not shortlist coverage

`verified` · `@bpg.assessment.slow-canonical-switch-interpretation/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/stillsearch/**"`

On the sampled image, the main architectural risk was not rough
shortlist coverage; it was finalizing the cheap top-1 winner too
early. Serious SIMD work should optimize the exact-evaluation path
because the more x265-shaped search spends much more time in exact
prediction and transform.

**supported_by** `@bpg.observation.simd-audit-work-buckets/1`

> **At risk** at depth 1 via `supported_by` → `@bpg.observation.simd-audit-work-buckets/1` (stale: `watches "crates/still265/src/encoder/**"` was matched by `0cfa2afe`, which touched `crates/still265/src/encoder/stillsearch/canvas.rs`.). See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#the-architectural-risk-was-early-cheap-top-1-finalization-not-shortlist-coverage).

### Wide-SIMD intra predictors gave no measurable gain at the trial block sizes

`verified` · `@bpg.assessment.wide-simd-predictor-refuted/1` · scope `path "crates/still265/src/encoder/**"`

Honest result: no measurable gain from wide-SIMD prediction kernels
- trial blocks are 8x8/4x4-heavy, and 8-wide i32 lanes with scalar
u8 packing don't pay at those sizes (4x4 falls back to scalar
entirely). A later substage split found the wide predictors had
optimized the trivial part: border building was 4.77s (26%) of the
Predict substage, the prediction kernels themselves only 0.53s
(3%).

### psy_rd_weight matches x265's weighting shape

`verified` · `@bpg.evidence.psy-rd-shape-match/1`

The ported psy-rd energy weight kernel (factor = psy_rd * 0.33 *
(96.0/256.0), tapered above QP 40, zero at QP>=51) matches x265's
rdcost.h formula shape; env overrides BPG_PSY_RD (clamp 0..=5) and
BPG_PSY_RDOQ (clamp 0..=50) resolve as designed.
